agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager gets a candidate who already knows what GMP training records are for, names the gaps, and offers a concrete 90-day plan, so a phone screen is likely, though nothing proves plant readiness.

honest.reason: The letter drops the unsupported promise to halve training time, and every figure matches the brief; the only additions are a derived 'seven years' and a reasonable description of what Google Classroom does.

works_the_facts.reason: Most figures are repeated as given: the 41%→58% rise isn't stated as 17 points or a roughly 40% relative gain, and the safety record isn't totalled into roughly a thousand students over seven injury-free years.

right_comparison.reason: It compares teacher onboarding with new-hire training, which is fair, but it never sets the candidate against the realistic alternative (someone with GMP experience but less teaching skill) or describes the plant's current training as the facts show it.

qualification.reason: The hedges come with checkable commitments: a GMP course before the start date and a written, timed plan within 90 days, though it doesn't say what happens if either is missed.

objections.reason: The objection that teachers don't understand regulated plants is met directly, by explaining what GMP records are for and how the candidate would close the gap, and no objection is raised that the brief already answers.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right form; it leaves out the requested 'cut training in half' line, which is the right call, and it explains why.
